title: Estimating the autumn flow slope cut March log-flow error by 52% in 14 retained winters at three Arctic gauges in 1952-1975
abstract: We tested whether estimating the autumn flow slope improves March flow forecasts in an earlier Arctic river record. At Ob, Lena and Yenisey gauges, 14 common certified winters in 1952-1975 gave a 52.24% equal-river mean reduction in squared log-flow error against a fixed slope with a time trend. Conditional 95% three-year block limits were 31.56% to 58.46%. The gain over time alone was 0.43%, with limits of -46.12% to 19.94%. The last-15-training-winter comparison had limits that depended on block length. The 40.81% late-period gain from prior work was reproduced; the late-minus-early difference was uncertain. The early record supports relaxing a fixed proportional relation, but does not establish added autumn information beyond time. Sparse early coverage, revised data, regulation and conditional uncertainty limit transfer. Code, provenance, aggregate evidence, a figure and an arithmetic audit support reproduction. External source records and record-level tables remain outside the package.

display.caption: Early and late forecast gains against two reference models. Bars show conditional 95% three-retained-year block limits. The early test has 14 winters; the late test has 30.

citations.reason: Prior late-period forecast comparison defines the models. This study adds early targets; data and training years overlap.
